facts.text: RTX's Pratt & Whitney Canada is investing $275 million CAD in its Longueuil facility, with support from the Canadian and Quebec governments.
In 2025, Développement économique de l'agglomération de Longueuil (DEL) helped maintain or create 3,329 jobs and supported 975 businesses, with about $31.5 million in financing for local SMEs.
The Longueuil agglomeration is home to the École nationale d'aérotechnique, the largest aerospace technical training institution in North America.
facts.publisher: DEL - Développement économique de l'agglomération de Longueuil

facts.text: The Canadian Space Agency has its head office in Saint-Hubert, a borough of Longueuil.
Pratt & Whitney Canada, the RTL and Agropur, all based in Longueuil, appear on Forbes' list of Canada's best employers.

overview: Longueuil counted 254,483 residents in the 2021 Census, up 6.1 percent from 239,700 in 2016, a faster pace than Quebec as a whole. Those people live on 115.77 square kilometres on Montreal's South Shore, so a local business is competing in a dense, growing market rather than a sprawling one.

The economy leans on aerospace and public institutions. Pratt & Whitney Canada, the Canadian Space Agency and the École nationale d'aérotechnique anchor Saint-Hubert, and the local development agency actively finances small and medium businesses. Firms that speak to that skilled workforce and its suppliers have a clear audience.
